posts.author: kamimichiku_
posts.body:
Hello everyone. I’m currently developing a psychological horror game titled
Shadows of Thornhill
. It’s set in the quiet, fog-shrouded village of Ashford, where an ancient curse still lingers around the decaying Blackwood Manor, a place that has stood for centuries as a silent witness to something terrible.
I’ve been working hard on this project for some time, but I’ve reached a point where I really need help. I’ve been struggling to fix several technical issues and to understand some aspects of rpg maker mz's eventing and system setup. I’ve tried to learn and troubleshoot as much as I can on my own, but I’ve been stuck for a while now.
I’m looking for an
rpg maker mz dev
who would be willing to assist, either by helping me fix existing problems, guiding me through certain mechanics, or possibly joining the project as a collaborator. Any support would mean a great deal to me

posts.author: SGHarlekin
posts.body:
Hi there and welcome to the forum. Just a quick tip about “asking to ask”:  it means posting something like:
kamimichiku_ said:
I’m looking for an
rpg maker mz dev
who would be willing to assist, either by helping me fix existing problems, guiding me through certain mechanics
Click to expand...
without actually stating what the problem is.
Here’s why that is bad form:
It asks people to commit time and attention before knowing what your request really is, which can be off-putting.
It doesn’t give enough information for someone to decide whether they actually CAN help, so many won’t even bother.
It gives the impression you’re unwilling to do the groundwork yourself (like explaining your issue clearly) so others ask “why should we do the work?"
It wastes time and lowers your chances of getting a helpful response. If you instead state the exact technical problem, what you’ve tried, and what you expected vs what happened, you’ll get much better responses.
And if you're primarily looking for a collaborator,
@EpicFILE
has given the right section for that. (although that needs an entirely different post, not "I need help fixing my game")

posts.author: ZombieKidzRule
posts.body:
Welcome to the forum!
You might find the most luck if you start choosing one issue at a time that you struggling with and making a support post about it. If you give sufficient information about what you are trying to do, what is happening, where you are stuck, and provide screenshots of what you have so far, you are more likely (just in my opinion) to get assistance.
There are a lot of very helpful people on the forum who try to assist with individual support threads as they see them, but they might be less likely to want to do a sort of direct collaboration or direct tutorial thing.
I have made quite a few posts for help with individual issues here over the years with terrific results.
Anyway, just a thought.
You can PM me if you want, but I may or may not be able to help. That's the benefit of making a support post for everyone to see.
Good luck on your project and remember to enjoy what you do.
